newsitem.title: UK: German job crisis not due to EMU - EUs Brittan.
newsitem.headline: German job crisis not due to EMU - EUs Brittan.

text.p: The sharp rise in German unemployment has not been caused by the country's efforts to qualify for a single European currency, European Commissioner Leon Brittan said on Thursday.

"I don't (agree) at all that the current unemployment (in Germany) is the result of trying to meet the Maastricht criteria (on monetary union)," Brittan, a member of Britain's Conservative Party, told a news conference in London.
"It is caused by a failure to make structural changes that have been needed for some years."
Brittan, who was speaking at the launch of a pro-EU information campaign by Britain's European Movement, said he still expected the single currency to be launched on schedule on January 1, 1999.
He said the Maastricht criteria were forcing some EU governments into economic reforms which would lay the foundations for their future prosperity.
"Countries like Spain and Italy and others are embarking on the reforms which are needed to put their finances in order and lay the basis for long-term prosperity," he said.
But Brittan, Commissioner for External Trade, backed the British government's wait-and-see stance on the single currency.
"It seems to me to be wholly rational to keep the options open at the moment. There are still important decisions which have to be decided as to how the currency would work," he said.
He warned if Britain ruled out membership it would lose crucial influence.

"To absent oneself from the table by saying no' would be to deprive Britain of the opportunity to have influence on these decisions. It would be a crazy thing to do, and the government is absolutely right to keep its options open," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
